Locked in plan (weather‑suitable choice):

- Date: Sunday 28 December 2025  
- Time: 4:30 pm – 8:00 pm  
- Location type: Darwin foreshore/park with shade and easy parking

1) Location criteria (what to look for on the foreshore)  
When you scout options, aim for a spot with:
- Shade: trees and/or fixed shelters; space for a few pop‑up gazebos.  
- Parking: car park or plenty of on‑street parking within a short walk.  
- Facilities: toilets, taps, BBQs (or space for permitted portable BBQs), bins.  
- Space: one larger grass area where 40–60 people can gather, plus a nearby open area for kids’ games.  
- Safety: away from busy roads; good visibility of where kids will play; lighting nearby if possible as it gets dark.

(Examples to check locally: sections of Nightcliff Foreshore, East Point Reserve, Bicentennial Park, etc., choosing the exact node based on the above.)

2) Simple run‑sheet (4:30–8:00 pm)  
- 4:00–4:30 pm: Organiser set‑up (arrive early with a small crew).  
- 4:30–5:15 pm: Arrivals, free play, ice‑breaker (bubbles/chalk/balls for kids).  
- 5:15–6:15 pm: Main food time (BBQ / shared picnic table). Short welcome and any community announcements.  
- 6:15–7:15 pm: Light activities:
  - Kids: relay races, tug‑of‑war, scavenger hunt, frisbee.  
  - Adults/families: casual lawn games (Kubb, bocce, cricket).  
- 7:15–8:00 pm: Dessert/fruit, relaxed chatting, photos, gradual pack‑down.

3) Core equipment checklist (for 40–60 people)  
Group items:
- Shelter & seating: 2–4 pop‑up gazebos, 4–6 picnic rugs, 10–20 folding chairs.  
- Tables & food: 3–4 trestle tables, eskies with ice, serving utensils, rubbish/recycling bags.  
- BBQ/picnic: gas BBQs or confirm park BBQs work; tongs, gloves; paper towels, wipes, hand sanitiser.  
- Lighting & comfort: a couple of battery lanterns/headlamps for pack‑down, insect repellent, basic first‑aid kit.  

Food (simple approach):
- Mains: sausages/burgers/veggie patties + bread/rolls, simple salads.  
- Sides/snacks: fruit, chips, cut vegetables, dips.  
- Drinks: big water dispensers, cordial/juice, a simple system if BYO soft drinks is allowed.  
- Plates/cups/cutlery/napkins (aim for reusable/compostable where possible).

4) Activities suitable for mixed ages  
- “Any‑time” options: balls, frisbees, skipping ropes, giant bubbles, chalk drawing area.  
- 1–2 short structured moments:
  - Welcome + quick intro of organisers and purpose.  
  - One community game or raffle / prize draw (if appropriate).  

Next, I can help you with any of these in more detail:
- A short‑list of location types/features to send someone who’ll scout the foreshore.  
- A detailed packing list with approximate quantities for 40 vs 60 people.  
- A simple invite message you can email/post to the community with all key details.

Which would you like to work on next?</action>
